cards.text: Jesus has just gone back and forth with some Pharisees and scribes from Jerusalem about eating with unwashed hands (Matthew 15:1-20). Now He leaves that place and withdraws. New road, new district.

cards.question: Jesus leaves the argument about unwashed hands behind. Where does He withdraw to?

answers.text: The district of Tyre and Sidon

cards.text: A Canaanite woman from that region comes to Him, and friend, this is NOT an inside voice. She's CRYING OUT: "Lord, Son of David, have mercy on me!"

cards.question: What's going on that has the Canaanite woman crying out to Jesus for mercy?

answers.text: Her daughter is possessed by a demon
Her husband is sick with a fever
Her son has been blind from birth

cards.question: The Canaanite woman is begging Jesus to help her daughter. Jesus answers her right away.

cards.text: Not one word. Jesus stays silent, and that's when His disciples walk over to Him with a suggestion.

cards.question: The disciples urge Jesus to send the Canaanite woman away.
Why do the disciples want Jesus to send the Canaanite woman away?

answers.text: She keeps crying out after them
It is getting late in the day
The crowd is pressing in on them

cards.text: And then, after all that silence, Jesus speaks up. I'm leaning in like it's the last ten seconds on the oven timer.

cards.question: Jesus finally speaks. Who does He say He was sent only to?

answers.text: The lost sheep of the house of Israel
The scribes and elders of Jerusalem
The faithful ones in every nation

cards.question: After Jesus says He was sent only to the lost sheep of Israel, the Canaanite woman gives up and heads home.

cards.text: NOPE. She comes and kneels before Him and says, "Lord, help me!"
But Jesus replies, "It is not right to take the children's bread and toss it to the dogs." Now what is she going to say to that?

cards.question: The Canaanite woman answers Jesus' picture of the children's bread and the dogs. She says even the dogs get the ___ that fall from their master's table.

cards.text: She takes the very picture Jesus used and keeps right on asking. Friend, give me a HUNDRED more years in that junk drawer and I still don't come up with an answer like that.
Back in the Millers' kitchen, crumbs hit that floor EVERY SINGLE BATCH, and I never once saw one go to waste. Then Jesus answers her.

cards.question: She kept asking, even after Jesus' picture of the bread and the dogs. Jesus answers the Canaanite woman and tells her that her ___ is great.
Jesus tells the Canaanite woman, "Let it be done for you as you desire."
Jesus grants the Canaanite woman's request. When is her daughter healed?

findings.problem: The card makes the baker complete the woman's not-yet-presented reply by supplying the BSB word "crumbs." The blank is a near-verbatim continuation of verse 27, so it asks for the next wording of her line rather than testing a paraphrased meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin presents it as an actual recurring part of his past that crumbs hit the Millers' kitchen floor in every batch and that none was ever wasted. This adds a new incident and habit to his established backstory; the allowance for invented small moments and habits applies around his bakery.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The card makes the baker complete Jesus' not-yet-presented words, "your faith is great," by supplying "faith." Although the setup makes the answer plausible, the blank remains a next-word completion of the line rather than a meaning-based paraphrase.
